I immediately said, "Toybox." I knew it. And...same. I actually try, consciously, to NOT think about it.

And thank you for your empathy about Terry Schiavo. My grandmother was in the same hospice as Terry during the height of it all. We had to pull up during some of the hardest moments of our lives to people yelling and holding signs, and wade our way through that just to be with my grandmother as she tried to gracefully exit this life. It was a circus. And there was nothing graceful about the whole situation. 

We, going through our own things in that moment, weren't fully cognizant about everything that was happening, and weren't in any position to do any research, though we were aware of the news stories--so, oddly, I didn't even connect the man who was there EVERY DAY, being sweet with his wife, wheeling her out, talking softly to everyone, CLEARLY taking care of this woman he loved, with the fact that this was actually Terry Schiavo, the very woman that all this was about. I know that seems hard to believe, but we, and most other people trying to visit loved ones in that hospice facility (and they were wonderful), were truly grieving our own loved ones and living our own stories.

I won't ever forget it, and thank you for remembering and telling their story with such empathy.
